text: concern: pre-existing (not mine, outside FILES): `packages/tinyapp-exam/test/render-move.test.ts` fails 6 tests when run as its own `bun test` invocation — `Could not resolve: "@/components/ui/button"` (and input/checkbox) while bundling `client/index.html`. That drags down `packages/tinyapp-exam/test/browser-exam.test.ts` leg (f), which spawns exactly that invocation. Confirmed pre-existing by reverting `client/src/Store.tsx` and `client/src/storeData.ts` to BASE `7d578da` and re-running: the same 6 failures. Both files are outside this task's FILES and outside its PROOFS
the full `bun test` run with my changes is 537 pass / 2 fail, the 2 being this pair.

M7 ends on a teardown assertion for every failing species ("after every outcome above no child of the test process is a Chromium and a `fetch` from Bun to the exam's origin rejects"), and leg (g) prescribes the source of that origin as "read off `data-origin` in `record.dom`". For two of the six species — never-ready (`packages/tinyapp-exam/test/persistence-move.test.ts`, 'leg (g) [M7]: a page that never reports its persister is red on the ready wall') and never-persisting ('...rows that never match the store are red on the persist wall') — the walk in `packages/tinyapp-exam/src/persistence-move.ts` returns before `record.domBefore` or `record.dom` is ever set, so no markup and no `data-origin` exists to read. `assertClosed` therefore skips the `fetch`-rejects half for exactly those two (it guards on `originOf(record) !== null`), and only the "no Chromium child" half is established there. The server-stopped half is in fact honoured by the `finally` in `measure` (`server.stop(true)`), so this is a gap in what the exam can witness, not a defect in the tree: as leg (g) is written, no faithful implementation can assert it for a species whose record carries no page. Closing it would need the origin surfaced somewhere other than the DOM (e.g. an optional field on the outcome or record), which is a change to the helper's public shape the task does not ask for. Recorded so the operator knows M7's last clause is established for four of the six species rather than all six.

concern: plan-defect: the Proof's fifth `Run:` line — `bun test packages/tinyapp-exam/test/state-exam.test.ts packages/tinyapp-exam/test/evidence.test.ts packages/tinyapp-exam/test/render-move.test.ts` — is already red at BASE and this task cannot make it green. Measured in a detached worktree at 7d578da: 36 pass / 9 fail there, and 36 pass / 9 fail in this tree — identical test for test. Every failure is `Could not resolve: "@/components/ui/button"` (and siblings) out of `bundleOf`. Cause, reproduced minimally: under Bun 1.4.0 on this image, `Bun.build` inside a `bun test` process resolves tsconfig `paths` from the repository-root tsconfig only, and BASE commit 7d578da added `@/*` imports to `client/src/*` without a root tsconfig

the same build under `bun run`/`bun -e` succeeds because it walks to `client/tsconfig.json`. The task's own Context records its measurements under Bun 1.4.2, so this is plausibly a version difference rather than something anyone saw when 7d578da landed. Full-suite comparison, also identical: BASE 537 pass / 2 fail, this tree 537 pass / 2 fail

`bun test packages/tinyapp-lint packages/tinyapp-exam` 100 pass / 29 fail in both. A real fix belongs to whoever owns `client/` or the Bun pin: rewrite the `@/…` imports as relative, pin Bun 1.4.2, or add a root tsconfig *and* move the five `tsc`-shelling tests onto `--ignoreConfig`.

concern: out-of-FILES (not taken): adding a repository-root `tsconfig.json` mapping `@/*` to `./client/src/*`. Tried and measured: it does clear all 29 bundling failures and leaves `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint:state` and `bun run lint:ui` at 0, but a `tsconfig.json` in the root makes every `tsc` the suite spawns with files on its command line emit `error TS5112: tsconfig.json is present but will not be loaded if files are specified on commandline`, and five tests in `browser.test.ts` and its neighbours assert `tsc`'s output is empty — full suite 534 pass / 5 fail with it against 537 pass / 2 fail without. It trades nine reds for five different ones, so it is not a fix and was reverted
the tree carries no root tsconfig.

concern: The two `Test:` paths (`packages/tinyapp-exam/test/persistence-move.test.ts` and `tests/state-exams/persistence-exam.test.ts`) are untouched, per the brief, so M1's `bun run lint:state`-with-that-file-present and all of M8 are unverified from here. `bun run lint:state` exits 0 on this tree as it stands (0 findings over 20 snapshots and 24 exams), and the capture child links the three new names — checked separately — but the exact wording of M8's red-registration leg rests on the peer's exam.

concern: out-of-FILES (not taken): `tests/state-exams/styled-page.test.ts` leg (f) [M6] — which spawns `bun test packages/tinyapp-lint packages/tinyapp-exam` — is still red, the one survivor of the two [M6] meta-legs that were red at BASE. That child is now 127 pass / 17 fail (BASE: 100 / 29). The 17 are a different mechanism from the 12 this fix reached: `error: Cannot find module '@/components/ui/button' from client/src/TodoInput.tsx`, raised by Bun's *runtime* module loader when `loadContext()` dynamically imports the client modules run-22 gave `@/` imports — same missing `paths` map, a resolver no `Bun.build` option or bundler plugin can set. (Those lint files pass in the whole-suite run and when `packages/tinyapp-lint` runs alone

only this child combination is red.) Fixing it needs one of: rewriting `client/src/*`'s `@/…` imports to relative paths — blocked outright, since a Global Constraints Check pins `client/src/components`, `TodoItem.tsx`, `TodoList.tsx`, `TodoInput.tsx` and `index.tsx` byte-for-byte against BASE
or a runtime resolver plugin preloaded via `bunfig.toml`, out of FILES and repo-wide. None is in this task's FILES, and this leg is in no Proof `Run:` or Check of this task.

concern: unsatisfiable (recorded by the examiner, unchanged by this round): leg (g)'s never-ready species cannot assert the closed-origin fetch — a run that never reaches ready carries no `dom`, so the record has no `data-origin` and the exam cannot learn the OS-chosen port. The exam asserts the empty browser list for all six species and the closed-origin fetch for the five whose record carries a DOM.
